message.content: {"pharmakon_274e":{"rendering":"an elixir of memory and wisdom","gloss":"an elixir (of) memory and wisdom","category":"elixir/potion","note":"Fowler reorders the Greek: 'memory and wisdom' is a genitive dependent on 'elixir'. The word 'elixir' is the translator's choice; it is not a literal 'drug' or 'remedy'."},"mneme_274e":{"rendering":"memory","gloss":"memory","note":"Also rendered 'improve their memories' just before, where the Greek has the adjective μνημονικωτέρους."},"sophia_274e":{"rendering":"wisdom","gloss":"wisdom","note":""},"pharmakon_275a":{"rendering":"an elixir","gloss":"an elixir","category":"elixir/potion","note":"Same word as at 274e, so the repetition is preserved. The second 'elixir' is elliptical: the Greek φάρμακον is not repeated in the English clause 'not of memory, but of reminding'."},"mneme_275a":{"rendering":"memory","gloss":"memory","note":"Same word as at 274e."},"hypomnesis_275a":{"rendering":"reminding","gloss":"reminding (the act of being reminded)","note":"Verbal noun. It contrasts with 'memory', but the English gives no sense of ὑπό ('from under/prompting'), nor of the 'record/memorandum' sense."},"sophia_275a":{"rendering":"the appearance of wisdom, not true wisdom","gloss":"the appearance of wisdom, not true wisdom","note":"δόξα is rendered 'appearance', not 'opinion' or 'reputation'. ἀλήθεια ('truth') becomes the adjective 'true' modifying 'wisdom'. The opposition is appearance versus real wisdom."},"doxosophoi_275b":{"rendering":"not wise, but only appear wise","gloss":"not wise, but only appear wise","note":"The compound δοξόσοφοι ('wise-seeming') is unpacked into a clause, with no single word; the phrase ἀντὶ σοφῶν is turned into 'not wise, but only…'."},"argument":"Fowler keeps 'elixir' for both occurrences of φάρμακον, so Thamus does turn Theuth's own word against him, and the 'memory/reminding' contrast stays visible. But 'elixir' picks the magical-potion sense of the word and drops the medicine/poison ambivalence, and the second occurrence is elliptical, which weakens the verbal echo. The wisdom/appearance opposition is carried by plain English phrases, and the compound δοξόσοφοι vanishes into a clause."}
